title: Deduction Bases on the Keyturn Host Payout Account
content:
What the host owes is taken from the Keyturn Host Payout Account rather than invoiced, and every deduction names the basis it was taken on so that the host can see what it was for.

## The separate bases

The marketplace commission on each trip, the protection fee the plan charges and any claim deductible the host owes are separate deductions, and none of them is netted against another before it reaches the statement. Restated at the level of a single statement: a host who owes commission, a protection fee and a deductible in the same month sees three lines, not one combined figure.

## A guest chargeback while it is disputed

A chargeback a guest raises is held against the host at the schedule's chargeback share while it is disputed, and where the dispute is lost the marketplace recovers it inside the schedule's recovery window; where it is won the hold is released in full.

| Outcome of the dispute | What happens to the sum held |
|---|---|
| The dispute is lost | The marketplace recovers it inside the schedule's recovery window |
| The dispute is won | The hold is released in full |

## Correcting a deduction

A deduction posted in error is corrected by a correcting entry and never by editing the entry that was wrong.

## Clauses no longer in force

Two clauses of these deduction bases have been withdrawn and are no longer in force; neither is applied:

> "Transfer fees are deductions in their own right and are taken on the day the transfer goes out, so a host who asks for money quickly sees the cost of speed on the same statement line day as the payout itself."

> "A deduction never takes the account below zero on the entry that causes it, but where it does the balance stands negative and the marketplace recovers the schedule's share of each later earning until it is cleared, beginning only once the schedule's grace period in whole calendar days from the day the balance went negative has run."
